solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: All the best beer good to take on holiday

indicators.note: the holiday word takes the following pieces on after it

parts.note: a short holiday is a break
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone recommends packing beer for a good holiday, wishing all the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take on' means the holiday takes the beer and good on after it, not around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatrical idiom wishing a performer good luck, said in place of a plain good wishes phrase.

clue.text: Hit head on mirror entering tavern the wrong way

indicators.note: the first letter of mirror goes inside the reversed tavern word
in a down clue, the tavern word is read backwards, the wrong way up

parts.note: a pub is a tavern

indicators.note: the head of the word mirror is its first letter

explanation.surface: A drunk stumbles backwards through a pub and bangs their head on a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns PUB into BUP; 'entering' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to knock into something is to strike or hit it.

clue.text: Genius, Humpty Dumpty?

definitions.meaning: the nursery-rhyme character is drawn as an egg with a face, literally an egg for a head

explanation.surface: Was the nursery-rhyme egg Humpty Dumpty secretly a genius?
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an intellectual, and the question mark flags the literal reading of the egg-shaped character.

clue.text: In hock, I need family

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words hock, I need

explanation.surface: A debtor with things at the pawnbroker's turns to their family for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hock' means in debt, but 'In' is the signal that the answer is concealed in hocK I Need.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: relatives or blood relations are one's family.

clue.text: Songs heard — Queen, possibly?

indicators.note: the word for the songs is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: lieder are German art songs

explanation.surface: Are those songs heard sung by the Queen, perhaps?
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a queen is a head of state, one who leads, flagged by 'possibly'.

clue.text: Sponsor daren't go splashing out, penny saved

indicators.note: the rearranged letters keep the penny safely inside them
splashing out suggests things scattered about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sponsor is too cautious to spend, saving every penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashing out' rearranges DARENTGO into GODARENT; 'saved' holds P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent sponsors a child at baptism, vouching for their religious upbringing.

clue.text: That thing follows start of football match

indicators.note: the pronoun comes after the first letter
the start of the word football is its first letter

parts.note: it is the pronoun for that thing

explanation.surface: Something happens right after the start of a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to suit or correspond, as when colours go together.

clue.text: Distant limits of Swahili language

parts.note: far means distant

indicators.note: the limits of the word Swahili are its outer letters

explanation.surface: The far edges of the Swahili-speaking world are described as distant limits of the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Persian, the language spoken in Iran, is also known by this name.

clue.text: Difficult responsibility of judge and jury?

definitions.meaning: judge and jury are charged with hearing a case in court

explanation.surface: The courtroom job of judge and jury is a hard one.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for tiresome, and the verb for hearing a case in court.

clue.text: Rep entertained by mother a shade

indicators.note: the rep word is held inside the mother word, as a guest is entertained by a host

parts.note: ma is mother
a rep or representative is an agent

explanation.surface: A sales rep is invited in and entertained by someone's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A purplish-red colour, so one example of a shade.

clue.text: Communist returns via English city

indicators.note: the communist word is read backwards

parts.note: a red is a communist
by means via, as in by way of

explanation.surface: A communist comes back to England through one of its cities.
explanation.walkthrough: DERBY is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the East Midlands of England, also famous for horse racing.

clue.text: Thought freedom found by outsiders in diocese

indicators.note: the freedom word is placed beside the outside letters
the outside letters of the word diocese

parts.note: liberation is freedom

explanation.surface: Freedom is discovered by outsiders within a church diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: careful consideration or reflection is thought.

clue.text: Extraordinary reduction present

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop offers an extraordinary price cut on a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb senses: to present a speaker is to bring them forward and make them known.

clue.text: Change in speed, I think

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words speed, I think

explanation.surface: Someone muses that there has been a change in pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to revise or alter a text is to change it.

clue.text: TV award bowls me over — good Lord!

indicators.note: the word me is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise like good Lord!

explanation.surface: An awards winner gasps that the TV prize has completely bowled them over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowls' is padding for the surface; 'over' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: The US prize for television achievement, the small-screen counterpart of the Oscars.

clue.text: Cosmetic — half made to cover a blemish

indicators.note: the first pieces go round the blemish word, covering it
half of the word made is its first two letters

parts.note: a scar is a blemish

explanation.surface: Makeup applied half-heartedly to hide a spot on the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blemish' reads as one unit, but the A joins half of 'made' and the two go round the blemish from either side.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: eyelash make-up is one cosmetic.

clue.text: Who sat fidgeting? Who cares?

indicators.note: fidgeting suggests restless movement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks who sat there fidgeting, and someone else shrugs it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive retorts saying the matter is of no importance.

clue.text: Very damp old township in South Africa

parts.note: so means very
wet means damp

explanation.surface: A soggy old settlement in South Africa is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The large township near Johannesburg, famous in the anti-apartheid struggle.

clue.text: T-shirt on to do exercises, one producing a lovely smile

indicators.note: exercises suggests the letters are put through their paces and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pulls on a T-shirt to work out, grinning happily.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist specialising in straightening teeth, whose braces give patients a better grin.

clue.text: Country cousin ultimately dressed in Roman garb

indicators.note: the letter is wrapped in the garment

parts.note: a toga was the garment of ancient Rome

indicators.note: the last letter of the word cousin

explanation.surface: A country cousin turns up dressed in a toga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country cousin' reads as one phrase, but 'Country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Pacific island kingdom is a country.

clue.text: Bet volcano is elevated

indicators.note: in a down clue the volcano name is lifted up, read from bottom to top

parts.note: Etna is the volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: A gambler wagers on whether a volcano will rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker term: the stake put in before cards are dealt.

clue.text: Devout Indian, uniform on back

indicators.note: the uniform letter is placed on the back word

parts.note: hind means back, as in hind legs
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A religious Indian wears a uniform on their back.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the main religion of India, so one devout Indian.

clue.text: Formerly common excuse

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
plain means common or ordinary

explanation.surface: An excuse that was once the usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb senses: to justify or account for a fault, as in explaining something away.

clue.text: Starter of pastry that is — for this?

definitions.text: Starter of pastry that is — for this?

indicators.note: the starter of the word pastry is its first letter

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Is pastry the first course required for this dish?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: pastry is what you start with to make one.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked dish with a pastry crust, for which pastry is the starting point.

clue.text: Drink a drop, shortly

indicators.note: the drop word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a tear is a drop from the eye

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a quick drop of something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the British hot brew is a drink.

clue.text: Clear body of text I assess

indicators.note: the body of the word text is its middle letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to rate is to assess

explanation.surface: A marker reviews the body of a text and clears it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to absolve someone of blame is to clear them.
